title: DOE Releases Genesis Agent Skills to Support AI-Driven Scientific Research
source_used: ExecutiveGov (reporting a US Department of Energy announcement)
key_facts: The US Department of Energy published Genesis Agent Skills, technical resources to help researchers and developers use AI coding tools for scientific research.
DOE said Thursday (15 Oct 2026) it is the first set of resources from ModCon and the American Science Cloud to support the Genesis Mission.
It was built by ModCon's Baseline AI R&D Capabilities team (BASE), co-led by Nathan Hodas of PNNL and Stefan Wild of Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory.
It covers AI safety, agent evaluation and monitoring, data governance, scientific workflows and multi-agent systems.
Users can ask AI coding tools plain-language questions for technical guidance or code reviews drawing on Genesis Mission guidance.
It is free on GitLab and DOE invites users to adapt workflows and contribute.
Court Corley, interim technical director of the Genesis Mission and a senior scientist at PNNL, says the aim is expertise in a form that is accessible, reusable and ready to support new work.
quote_evidence: DOE said Thursday that the package is the first set of resources developed through ModCon: Transformational AI Models and Data and the American Science Cloud to support the Genesis Mission.
Researchers, developers and the public can access the package free of charge on GitLab, where DOE is inviting users to browse the catalog, adapt the workflows and contribute enhancements.
why_it_matters_hint: Shared national-laboratory guidance for AI-assisted research, free to use.
